name: Shruti
description: That which is heard — the eternal, revealed scriptures comprising the four Vedas and their ancillary texts, considered to be of divine origin and uncreated.

name: Smriti
description: That which is remembered — the body of texts considered to be of human authorship and secondary authority, including the Itihasas, Dharmashastra, and related literature.

name: Purana
description: Ancient lore — eighteen major texts (Mahapuranas) and numerous minor texts (Upapuranas) narrating cosmogony, genealogies, mythology, and devotional teachings.

name: Vedanga
description: Limbs of the Veda — six auxiliary disciplines essential for the correct recitation, understanding, and preservation of the Vedic corpus.

name: Upaveda
description: Secondary Vedas — four traditional bodies of knowledge appended to the main Vedas: Ayurveda, Dhanurveda, Gandharvaveda, and Arthashastra.

name: Darshana
description: Vision or philosophical perspective — the six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy (Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Samkhya, Yoga, Mimamsa, Vedanta) and their sub-traditions.

name: Agama
description: Traditions that have come down — a large body of scriptures forming the basis of Shaiva, Shakta, and Vaishnava tantric and temple worship traditions.

name: Deity
description: Divine beings — the gods, goddesses, and divine manifestations of the Hindu tradition, from the supreme formless Brahman to specific forms worshipped in ritual.

name: Sage
description: Seers and sages — the rishis, acharyas, and teachers who received, transmitted, or systematised the sacred knowledge of the Hindu tradition.

name: Concept
description: Foundational ideas — the key philosophical, metaphysical, and soteriological concepts that form the intellectual backbone of Hindu thought.

name: Science and Art
description: The traditional sciences and arts — astronomy, mathematics, music, sculpture, dance, and other classical disciplines rooted in the Vedic and Agamic traditions.
